summary: Avoid inventing a deterministic order between top-level setTimeout(0) and setImmediate when Node does not guarantee one.

requirements.scheduling_context: top-level or otherwise not proven I/O poll callback

target.notes: Use the Node-compatible event-loop runtime; do not map ordering to arbitrary Task/ThreadPool scheduling.

semantics.ordering: host/event-loop context dependent; no source-level fixed order may be assumed
semantics.timer: 0 ms is a threshold/minimum-delay request, not synchronous

caveats: Node/libuv version and surrounding I/O can affect which becomes eligible first.
A translator must not constant-fold this pair into a hard-coded callback order.

tests.name: do not assert top-level winner
tests.expected_behavior: both callbacks eventually run; translation must preserve Node runtime scheduling rather than require one fixed order

tests.name: contrast with I/O context
tests.expected_behavior: inside the I/O callback a separate rule guarantees immediate before timeout
